title: arrowheadr
text: Teun van den Brand’s ggarrow package gives us ability make great-looking arrows ggplot2. Figure 1, make base_plot convenient reuse plot single arrow geom_arrow. Figure 1 particularly like arrow functions can resect arrows can put little space arrows objects connect.  can make arrowheads supplying arrow_head parameter 2-column matrix polygon points. ’ll make simple triangle:  can make shape want. made arrowheadr facilitate getting complex shapes box ggarrow functions expect. arrowheadr functions depend ggarrow, designed used ggarrow. main arrow_head_* functions return matrix columns x y create polygon fitting square −1 1 x y axes. main arrow_head_* functions optional plot argument show polygon used:  pink rectangle shows arrow’s line end. Typically, arrowhead’s point expected (1,0), can anything want. can now use output ggarrow:
code: library(arrowheadr) library(ggarrow) library(ggplot2) library(ggforce) library(tibble) library(dplyr) library(ggdiagram)  # Make simple plot for reuse base_plot <- data.frame(x = c(0, 1), y = c(0, 1)) |>   ggplot(aes(x, y)) +   coord_equal()  base_plot +   geom_arrow() base_plot +   geom_arrow(resect = 5) +   geom_point(size = 8) triangle <- cbind(x = c(1, 0, 0),                    y = c(0, .5, -.5))  base_plot +   geom_arrow(arrow_head = triangle) library(arrowheadr) my_arrowhead <- arrow_head_deltoid(plot = TRUE) base_plot +   geom_arrow(arrow_head = my_arrowhead)

title: Make Custom Arrowheads
text: ggarrow package makes possible create wide variety arrows. arrowheadr package makes easy create custom arrowheads.  ggdiagram package also uses arrowheadr ggarrow hood.
code: tibble(theta = seq(0,300, 60) * pi / 180,            x = cos(theta),            y = sin(theta)) |>   ggplot(aes(x, y)) +   coord_equal() +    geom_arrow_segment(aes(xend = x, yend = y, x = 0, y = 0), arrow_head = arrow_head_deltoid(), resect = 2) # Make a circle A <- ob_circle(center = ob_point(0, 0),                   radius = 1)  # Make angles evenly spaced around a circle theta <- degree(seq(0,330, 30))  # Make ring of points around the circle p <- ob_point() |>    place(from = A,          where = theta,         sep = 2)  # Make rotated squares B <- ob_rectangle(center = p, angle = theta)   ggdiagram() +    A +    B +    # Arrows from A to B   connect(A, B, resect = 2) +    # Straight arrows from B to adjacent B   connect(B@north, B[c(2:12, 1)]@south, resect = 2) +    # Arc arrows from B to adjacent B   connect(B[c(2:12, 1)]@east, B@east, arc_bend = -1, resect = 2)

code: # A normal distribution xy <- arrow_head_function(dnorm, plot = TRUE)  # if closed = FALSE, set thickness and base_width xy <- arrow_head_function(dnorm, plot = TRUE, closed = FALSE,                     thickness = 1.5,                     base_width = .25)   # A cauchy distribution xy <- arrow_head_function(dt, df = 1, plot = TRUE)  # open with thickness = 1.5 xy <- arrow_head_function(   dt,   df = 1,   plot = TRUE,   closed = FALSE,   thickness = 1.5 )  # thickness > 2 creates a bulge xy <- arrow_head_function(   dt,   df = 1,   lower_bound = -3.25,   upper_bound = 3.25,   closed = FALSE,   thickness = 2.5,   plot = TRUE,   rescale = 1 / 3,   nudge = c(2 / 3, 0) )   # Make a new function mytrident <- function(x, s = 160) {   k <- length(x)   y1 <- dbeta(x, shape1 = s, shape2 = s) * 2   y2 <- dbeta(x, shape1 = s * .9, shape2 = s * .1)   y3 <- dbeta(x, shape1 = s * .1 , shape2 = s * .9)   y1 + y2 + y3 }  xy <- arrow_head_function(   mytrident,   lower_bound = 0,   upper_bound = 1,   plot = TRUE,   minimum_value = -3,   rescale = .5,   nudge = c(.5, 0) )
